retained: Restore the chosen recording, queue, origin and usable playback position in a paused dock; restoring metadata does not open streams or activate audio.
The checkpoint carries its current recording independently of the queue, retaining a substitute source when queue membership no longer matches.
Unknown duration permits a positive finite position; a position within the last two seconds of a known duration resumes from zero.
An idle player or profile switch does not erase the previous profile's checkpoint.
Periodic two-second writes and pause, queue and app-inactivity flushes; storage failure does not interrupt playback.
mobileAdaptations: Profile-owned protected atomic files in Application Support replace IndexedDB and localStorage; catalog cache pressure cannot evict the checkpoint.
Queue metadata is serialized only when its revision changes, on a dedicated actor; ordinary time updates write a small checkpoint.
Remote resolved stream URLs and HTTP headers are not persisted. Configured direct/local recording references follow the existing owned playlist metadata policy.
Activation, resolver identity, cancellation and player request fences reject a late restore after profile change or a new play request.
The native bootstrap reads the checkpoint asynchronously and constructs the music workspace only when saved metadata exists.
OS force termination may precede an inactivity flush; the last completed atomic checkpoint remains usable.
